subject: Post-call: Availability gap analysis & SLO alignment (BlueStone Capital)
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Erin Brooks <erin@bluestonecap.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Availability gap analysis & SLO alignment (BlueStone Capital)

Erin — thanks for the time today. Quick recap of what we heard and what we propose as next steps. I wrote this to make sure we’re aligned before the technical deep dive.

Summary of pain points (as stated on the call)
- Repeated production degradations over the last 6 months; recent regional outage caused ~4 hours of elevated error rate.
- When capacity is constrained, their current fallback (smaller hosted model) produces unacceptable hallucination rates for credit decisioning flows.
- No automated, tested graceful-deg behavior — failovers sometimes route to incompatible model flavors or different regions causing data residency concerns.

Success criteria BlueStone outlined
- P99 latency target for inference endpoints: <= 400ms under normal load.
- Recovery time objective: <= 10 minutes for routing failovers (automated), <= 4 hours for manual remediation.
- Maintain decision-quality thresholds on fallback: false-positive rate for fraud/credit checks must not increase by >2% when fallback is active.
- Clear audit trails for any cross-region routing (data residency constraints).

What we observed (from the call)
- Current stack: in-house API gateway in front of a mix of vendor-hosted LLM and self-hosted inference; buddying vendor is used as a soft-fallback.
- Three incidents in last 6 months (one regional provider incident, one model OOM, one network blip) — customer willing to share incident timelines.

Redwood proposal (high level)
- Dedicated capacity baseline in US-East + warm standby in EU-West for cross-region failover (configurable per route and dataset).
- Canary and policy-based graceful degradation: route to lighter quantized model only after automated downstream validation (confidence thresholds + business-rule gating).
- Automated prefix/KV caching for the decisioning paths to reduce load and surface P99 improvements.
- Transparent SLO/SLA mapping in Console (per route token cost + latency histograms + token-level tracing) so BlueStone can audit changes during failovers.

Attachments included: MAP-v1.xlsx (initial mutual action plan), arch-diagram.png (proposal sketch), incident-timeline.csv (request template)

Open questions for your team (please reply inline if convenient)
1) Current steady-state QPS (3rd- and 95th-percentile)? expected peak concurrency?
2) Which flows are allowed to cross-region during failover (list of route names)?
3) Data residency / encryption requirements we should pre-configure for EU failover?

Proposed next step
- Technical deep-dive to scope Dedicated config, routing policy, and validation hooks. We have availability on Tue May 25 or Wed May 26, 60–90m. I added a tentative slot here: https://calendar.redwood.com/raf/deep-dive-20260525

Thanks again — I’ll wait for the incident timeline and answers to the three questions above.

— Rafael Mendes

From: Erin Brooks <erin@bluestonecap.com>

Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Availability gap analysis & SLO alignment (BlueStone Capital)

Thanks, Rafael — appreciate the clear notes. Confirming and adding details from our side.

Incident history (short list)
- 2026-03-18: Provider network blip — ~45 minutes of elevated latency, automatic retries masked some errors but user-facing timeouts rose by ~12%.
- 2026-04-02: Model OOM during a batch update — resulted in ~30% error rate for ~90 minutes on one critical route.
- 2026-05-09: Regional cloud provider outage (us-west) — approx 4 hours of degraded results; our current fallback switched to vendor-hosted smaller model which increased false positives on the credit-check flow.

Current stack and constraints
- API gateway (custom) -> routing to either our internal inference tier (self-hosted on reserved VMs) or vendor-hosted LLM.
- Data residency: EU data must remain within EU region unless explicitly allowed by compliance (we’ll mark routes); PII is encrypted at rest.
- Validation: we have limited automated downstream validators for the decisioning flows (mostly simple heuristics today).

Requirements for any fallback behavior
- No silent quality regressions for decisioning flows. If fallback model is used, it must pass the downstream validation pipeline or trigger a human review.
- Full audit trail for routing decisions and model variant used for every transaction.

We can share the incident timeline CSV — attaching the entries you requested. We’re available for the Tue May 25 deep-dive (10:00–11:30 PT) or Wed May 26 (13:00–14:30 PT).

For the POC we prefer: Dedicated capacity in us-east (primary) with eu-west warm standby. The POC acceptance criteria: maintain pre-POC decision-quality on 95% of sampled traffic, and demonstrate automatic failover + audit logs.

Erin Brooks
VP, Platform Engineering
BlueStone Capital
erin@bluestonecap.com

Looping in a short internal plan of attack based on Erin’s reply.

High-level plan (internal)
- Technical deep-dive attendees: runtime engineer (me), infra architect (Marissa), solutions engineer (Rafael).
- Scope for deep-dive: current request rate, exact routes + PII gating, candidate model variants + quantization profiles, routing policy (primary -> warm standby -> vendor-hosted as last resort).
- POC proposal: 2-week Dedicated trial in us-east with eu-west warm standby; automated canary (10% traffic) -> ramp to 100% on success; downstream validation hook required for decisioning routes.

Action items and owners
